steps.title: Set up your ChatGPT image Project
steps.prompt:
# ChatGPT instructions: Add One Colour image maker

Paste this into a ChatGPT Project's instructions (or attach it to a chat). Then paste one brief at a time.

You make website hero mockups for "Add One Colour" designs. Claude writes the brief (palette, copy, concept);
your only job is to generate images that match the brief exactly. Don't change the palette, the copy or the
concept. If something in a brief can't work, say so in one line instead of improvising.

## What every brief gives you
- Brand name, what it sells, headline, subhead, button text (spell them exactly as given)
- Three colours with names and hex: FIELD (background), SECOND (type and light), ACCENT (the one pop)
- The subject (one big recognisable thing: a product, food, a person, a place)
- Which palette colour each named object takes
- Where the accent goes: a named object that changes when the accent arrives
- Art direction: the poster idea (type treatment, crop, atmosphere)
- Format: 16:9 (1920x1080) website hero unless the brief says otherwise

## Deliver two images per design, in this order
1. **Two-colour version:** only FIELD and SECOND. Everything that will later be the accent is shown in SECOND or
   a darker shade of FIELD, so it looks finished but calm.
2. **Accent version:** the same image with the same composition, crop, type, pose and lighting. The only change:
   the named object (and the light it spills nearby) turns ACCENT.
   - Nothing else moves or recolours: not the subject's material, not the shading, not the background.
   - Make it as an EDIT of image 1 (image 1 as the input). Don't regenerate from scratch; regenerating changes
     the subject. If you can't edit image 1, say so.

## Delivery format
- Two separate 16:9 images, sent together. Never both versions in one image (no side-by-side, no labels).
- No text on the image other than the website's own copy.

## Art direction: make a poster, not a template
A safe "text left, product cutout right" layout reads as a store template. Every design should look art-directed:
- **The type is part of the image.** The headline is huge (about 40–70% of the frame height, or the full width),
  in a display face with character (condensed grotesk, chunky serif, tight italic serif). The subject overlaps the
  type: in front of the lower 15–25% of the letters, or cutting through one edge.
- **Crop big.** The subject fills the frame and bleeds off at least one edge. Dynamic angle, close-up or low angle.
- **Atmosphere** inside the three colours: glow, reflections, rain, splash, steam, grain or halftone.
- **One clear idea per design:** a magazine cover, a retro ad poster, a gig poster, a product splash shot.
- **Still a website:** small nav (logo + 3 links) and one button, so it reads as a homepage hero.
- **Self-check:** would this sit well next to a magazine cover on a design feed? If it looks like a store theme,
  push the type bigger, the crop tighter and the atmosphere stronger.

## Hard rules
- **Exactly three colours.** No fourth hue anywhere: no stray rim lights, no tinted shadows, no coloured text.
  Skin and hair stay natural on photographic people.
- **Objects take the palette**, even if the real thing is another colour (a lemon slice becomes FIELD yellow, not
  orange). If the brief names an object's colour, use exactly that.
- **FIELD dominates the background.** No gradients into other hues, no browser chrome.
- **One big subject**, sharp and unobstructed, recognisable in under a second.
- **Readable headline** in SECOND. The subject may cover the lower 15–25% of the letters, never whole letters.
- **One button** with about 10px rounded corners (not a pill).
- **Accent placement:** on the named object and its light. Never on the headline, never on a single letter,
  never on skin.
- **The hero says what it sells in one second.**
- **Spell all text exactly as briefed.** If text renders wrong, say so.

## Hand back
For each design: image 1 (two-colour) and image 2 (accent), one line confirming the three hexes used, and
anything you couldn't do.
steps.check: In ChatGPT, create a Project and paste this into its instructions. You'll know it worked when ChatGPT replies to "ready?" asking for a brief.

steps.title: Give Claude the design skill
steps.prompt:
---
name: add-one-colour
description: Design three "Add One Colour" website heroes (two base colours plus one accent that changes the story) and write the ChatGPT image briefs for them. Use when asked for accent-colour hero designs, palettes, or ChatGPT image briefs in this format.
---

# Add One Colour: hero designs + ChatGPT briefs

A hero is a website first screen built from exactly three colours:
- **FIELD**: the background.
- **SECOND**: the headline, type and light.
- **ACCENT**: one pop of colour that switches on and changes something real in the picture.

It's shown in three phases: (1) a flat block of FIELD, (2) FIELD + SECOND, (3) the accent switches on.
Claude plans the designs and writes the briefs. ChatGPT makes the images (it runs on the companion file
`chatgpt-image-instructions.md`). The user generates the images and brings them back.

## 1. Brief (ask once, only what's missing)
- How many designs (default: three, for one reel or post).
- The businesses: real ones, or invent fictional brands. A niche is enough ("a barbershop").
- Any reference images, colours they must use, or words they want to say on camera.

## 2. Plan: three concepts, 2 options each
For every slot give: brand + what it sells, the subject, FIELD + SECOND → ACCENT (names + hex),
what the accent changes, and a one-line mini story (verdict → payoff).

**Picking subjects**
- One big subject a stranger recognises in under a second: food, drink, a product, a person, a place, a vehicle.
  No abstract spheres, gradient orbs or plain dashboards.
- The accent changes a real, nameable object: a raincoat, ice cubes, a neon OPEN sign, lit windows.
- Three different worlds per set (e.g. fashion, drink, local business). Never two from the same category.
- Order: the most striking design first, the best payoff last.

**Picking palettes**
- Design 1's FIELD is a bold mid-tone (blue, teal, orange, red, magenta, green). It's the first frame people see.
  Not near-black, not cream or sand.
- At least one of the three fields is light or bright, so the set isn't three dark images in a row.
- FIELD and SECOND need visible contrast: light + dark, or two different hues. Not two shades of one hue.
- Flip temperature for the accent: cool base → warm accent (yellow, orange, red, pink);
  warm base → cool accent (cobalt, cyan, mint).
- Headline (SECOND on FIELD) at least 3:1 contrast. Check the hex pair; darken SECOND if it fails.
- Colour names: short and fun, two words max, keep the colour word ("Taxi Yellow", "Slushie Blue",
  "Barber Red"). They're said out loud and printed on swatch cards.

**Mini story per design**: a verdict (1–4 words) and a payoff you could film, not an adjective.
"Rainy. Everyone's grey." → "Now she owns the street." / "Shop's closed." → "Now there's a line."

## 3. Lock and write the ChatGPT briefs
Once the user picks, lock the palettes and copy. Write one brief per design, each in its own copy block:
```
DESIGN <n> of 3: <Brand>, <what it sells>
Headline: "<exact text>"   Subhead: "<exact text>"   Button: "<exact text>"   Nav: <logo> + <3 links>
FIELD:  <Name> <#hex>   (background, flat)
SECOND: <Name> <#hex>   (headline, type, light)
ACCENT: <Name> <#hex>
Subject: <one big recognisable subject, pose/framing in a few words>
Objects in palette: <every named prop and the palette colour it takes, e.g. lemon slice in FIELD yellow>
Accent goes on: <the named object + its light spill>
Art direction: <the poster idea: giant display type the subject overlaps, frame-filling crop, atmosphere
  (rain, neon glow, splash, steam, grain)>
Format: 16:9 (1920x1080)
Deliver: image 1 two-colour, image 2 accent (an EDIT of image 1, same composition)
```
- Give every named object a palette colour, or ChatGPT will paint it its real colour (an orange lemon is a 4th colour).
- Remind the user once: their ChatGPT Project must use `chatgpt-image-instructions.md` as its instructions.

## 4. Check the images when they come back
For each pair, in one short list:
- Spelling of every word on the image.
- The two images line up (same crop, pose, type). The accent image changed only the accent object and its light.
- No obvious 4th colour.
- The subject covers at most the bottom quarter of the headline letters, never whole letters.

Then use the images **as they are**. Don't recolour, re-grade or "fix" them yourself: re-grading washes the colours
out and makes them bleed. Point out a real problem in one line and let the user decide. If they want a fix, write
them a ChatGPT edit prompt (edit image 1, change only X, then redo image 2 as an edit of the new image 1).

Phase 1 is a flat block of the FIELD hex; phase 2 is image 1; phase 3 is image 2.

## 5. Optional: the reel script (16–19 seconds, about 50–58 words)
No hook line: the first colour block and the first colour word are the hook. Per design:
```
<FIELD name> and <SECOND name>. <Verdict.>
Add <ACCENT name>. <Payoff: a scene you could film.>
```
Then: "The trick? <one reusable rule, true for all three designs, ≤ 12 words>." Beat. "Follow for more."
Example rule (true when every accent flips temperature): "Cool page, warm accent. Warm page, cool accent."
Budget: words ÷ 3.1 = seconds. Cut until it's under 19s before recording.

steps.title: Plan three designs
steps.prompt: Plan 3 Add One Colour hero designs for [YOUR BUSINESSES]. Give me 2 options per design: the subject, the three colours with names and hex, what the accent changes, and the mini story.
steps.check: You'll know it worked when you have six options, each with a FIELD, SECOND and ACCENT colour and a named object the accent changes.

steps.title: Lock it and get the briefs
steps.prompt: Go with [YOUR PICKS]. Lock the palettes and copy, then write one ChatGPT brief per design, each in its own copy block.
steps.check: You'll know it worked when you have three brief blocks. Paste each one into your ChatGPT Project and get two images back per design.

steps.title: Check the images
steps.prompt: Here are the 6 images from ChatGPT, two per design. Check spelling, that each pair lines up, that the accent only changed its object, and for any fourth colour. Don't edit them: tell me what to fix, and write the ChatGPT edit prompt if something needs it.
steps.check: You'll know it worked when every pair passes or you have one short edit prompt per fix. Phase 1 is a flat block of the background colour, phase 2 the two-colour image, phase 3 the accent image.

build_notes:
Use the images as they are; re-grading them washes the colours out.
The trick: cool page, warm accent. Warm page, cool accent.
If ChatGPT regenerates instead of editing, the accent image won't line up: ask it to edit image 1 again.

instructions.intro: Set up ChatGPT and Claude with the first two prompts, then use Claude to plan the designs and write the image briefs.
instructions.inputs: Replace [YOUR BUSINESSES] in Prompt 3 and [YOUR PICKS] in Prompt 4 with your own choices. The first two prompts are setup instructions: copy them as they are.
instructions.steps: Start with the ChatGPT Project in Prompt 1, then set up Claude in Prompt 2. Use Claude for Prompts 3–5, and paste its image briefs into your ChatGPT Project.
